A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RioRAG. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across the substantial reorganization. Specific ambiguities in method specification and dataset coverage are identified below.

before.justification: v1 reports original LongFact and RAGChecker experiments, component ablations, model-scaling and initialization comparisons, and training-dynamics analyses in Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and analyses and reports additional reward-scoring comparisons, computation timings, and a generative-reward ablation in Figure 1 and Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: The retrieval, GRPO, Markdown activation, three-stage nugget/checklist pipeline, and exponential length penalty remain. v2 explicitly defines checklist-coverage scoring and excludes reasoning tokens from scoring and length decay. Because v1 leaves its assessment prompt and response segmentation unspecified, the PDFs do not establish whether these are procedural changes or newly documented details.

E1.justification: ELI5 training and LongFact coverage remain unchanged. Both versions list the same four RAGChecker datasets, but v1 Appendix A says eight subsets were used, v2 Appendix B says four, and both result captions say ten domains. It is unclear whether coverage narrowed or the subset count was corrected.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator sets are unchanged, including DPO. Within the ablation comparison, however, v1's w/ Off-Line RL variant, explicitly described as DPO, is replaced by w/ Generative GRPO using a 32B generative reward model. v2 also compares generative rewards against RioRAG in Figure 1 and the runtime table.

E3.justification: The replacement ablation uses GRPO with a 32B scalar reward model instead of offline DPO, and the new timing experiment compares sequential, parallel, and asynchronous execution. v2 Appendix C also changes the stated irrelevant-noise-sensitivity definition from facts present in retrieved pages to facts irrelevant to retrieval. Unchanged benchmark scores do not establish that this metric revision involved recomputation.

E4.justification: Scaling, initialization, length-control analyses, and most component ablations are retained. v2 replaces the offline-learning ablation with a generative-reward comparison, adds an illustrative reward-repeatability and human-ranking comparison in Figure 1, and examines reward-computation overhead in Table 1. These are targeted additions within the existing evaluation scope.

E5.justification: New Figure 1 explicitly reports reward evaluations averaged over three runs with mean and variance, including error bars. This adds uncertainty reporting for reward scoring, not independent training runs. Main benchmark tables still lack uncertainty estimates, and Appendix A's statement about reporting random seeds supplies no actual seed configuration.

E6.justification: The main LongFact and RAGChecker tables are numerically unchanged. The offline-DPO ablation reporting average FR/ID of 57.7/98.1 is replaced by the generative-GRPO variant reporting 54.7/97.2; these are different settings, not a performance decline under matched conditions. v2 adds Figure 1's reward findings and runtimes of 1.19 seconds per sample for generative rewards versus 2.32, 0.98, and 0.72 for sequential, parallel, and asynchronous RioRAG.

T1.justification: v2 adds an explicit reasoning/answer decomposition, a mathematical checklist-coverage reward definition, and asymptotic cost expressions in Table 1. It retains the advantage normalization and length-decay formula but omits v1's full clipped GRPO objective with KL regularization. These are limited changes to formal specification; neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains informativeness-oriented RL with hierarchical nugget rewards for long-form RAG. v2 adds explicit claims about externally verifiable rewards, reduced reward sparsity, and smaller-model self-improvement without strong-teacher distillation, while deemphasizing v1's slow-thinking motivation. The benchmark-success claim and conclusion remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: New discussion explains checklist credit assignment, shorter verification contexts, and parallel/asynchronous efficiency, replacing v1's blanket statement of no additional computational complexity. The revised ablation is interpreted through generative-reward instability. New limitations acknowledge that factual rewards omit style, coherence, and readability, and that scaling beyond 32B was not examined; existing English-language and extraction-bias caveats remain.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands implementation documentation with complete Extract and MergeCluster prompts, token limits, clipping, entropy and KL settings, PPO update details, and sequence parallelism. However, it omits v1's eight-H800 hardware configuration, bfloat16 precision, rollout temperature, eight rollouts per input, and overall training-epoch limit. Shared batch size, learning rate, warmup schedule, and repository link remain.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises the literature base and positions RioRAG relative to rubric/checklist rewards and retrieval used as a training-time verifier. Section 3.3 newly discusses Rubrics as Rewards and two factuality-training papers. Numerous references are added, while earlier works including RARR and The Great Nugget Recall are removed. Publication updates to retained works are not counted as additions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the method and analysis prose are rewritten. Task formulation becomes a standalone section, related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, metric explanations move into Appendix C, and implementation documentation is reorganized. Dedicated Discussion and Limitations sections further change the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, substantially rearranging text, tables, figures, and captions. v2 adds the introductory reward-comparison figure, runtime table, and boxed prompt templates. The existing framework diagram and scaling, initialization, and training-dynamics plots are retained with resizing, relocation, and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 is easier to assess and partly reproduce because reward definitions, extraction/merging prompts, and optimization settings are more explicit. The generative-reward ablation and cost comparisons also address questions left open in v1. The net gain is limited: main benchmark evidence is unchanged, some useful hardware and rollout details disappear, and RAGChecker coverage remains inconsistent.
